title: Annotatio III §.I: Letters urge Concord and fraternity with Zwinglians before and at Augsburg — theologians refuse fundamental consensus
pass_a_gloss: with many letters given on that matter to Luther, Melanchthon, and Brentius, seriously urging Concord — both before the Augsburg Diet and in the Diet itself once convened — and fraternity to be entered into and kept with the Zwinglians, which letters stand in Chytraeus in the Acts with the Zwinglians, the said Theologians also being indignant and unwilling to acknowledge a fundamental consensus of faith of the Zwinglians with themselves.
pass_b_english: He wrote again and again to Luther, Melanchthon, and Brentius, pressing hard for Concord — both before the Augsburg Diet and while it sat — and for fraternity with the Zwinglians that would actually be kept.

Those letters are still in Chytraeus’s Acts with the Zwinglians; and the named theologians, for their part, were angry and would not admit that the Zwinglians shared with them a fundamental consensus of faith.
source_text: pluribus eam in rem ad Lutherum, Melanchtonem & Brentium datis literis, Concordiam, tàm ante Augustana Comitia, quàm in ipsis celebratis, & fraternitatem cum Zvinglianis ineundam servandamq; seriò suadentibus, quae exstant apud Chytraeum in Actis cum Zwinglianis, indignantibus quoq;, dictos Theologos, Consensum fidei fundamentalem Zwinglianorum secum, haud agnoscere velle.
